verdicts.note: Self-references 'all girls school' and being 'a girl' in engineering; clearly female.
Explicit: 'going from an all girls school in sixth form' = single sex.
On her DIS industrial placement now (started Sept, design engineer); placement year confirmed by context.
IMechE chartership route plus CAD/design work supports Mechanical & Manufacturing; inferential, medium fair.
Currently on placement as design engineer; clearly yes.
Leads benefits with 'the experience' and is enthusiastic about learning; quote alone is mild, keep medium not high.
'idea of how I need to operate in a working environment' directly maps to seeing what industry is really like.
'giving me a lot of focus on what I want to do next' plus 'if its bad I know where I don't wanna go' supports deciding future direction.
'a break from uni instead of being sat with books' directly maps to needing a break from education.
'a year off chartership' maps to year counting towards Chartership.
Quote is about secrecy complicating her dissertation titles, NOT that she wanted placement to help choose a final-year project; does not support finalyr.
'I was interested in it so I'm becoming an engineer' directly supports interest as a draw.
'definitely at the right place, there's no humming and arring about it' strongly affirms being pleased; strongly agree justified.
Early theory 'not really doing much' for her work loosely supports difficulty seeing relevance; she also calls theory necessary, so low confidence appropriate.
Her personal tutor is also placement tutor; she emails him and he sorts problems, modestly supporting satisfied; low confidence fair.
'people have said but you're a girl, it's a strange degree' is a remark she explicitly rejects/never internalised; she names no one who tried to put her off. Not discouragement.
Falls with discoura; underlying discouragement not established, so identifying a discourager is unsupported.
'always wanted to do research or something hands on' plus 'research based placement' supports research/development.
'involved in projects rather than the managerial aspect' = rejecting managerial, leaving technical/specialist; medium fair.
Wanting to stay in home area where the firms are based implies location matters somewhat; thin, low confidence appropriate.
Quote merely describes the company's graduate/chartership programme structure; does not express that Chartership is important to her personally (elsewhere conditional 'if you want to do that').
